task_instruction:
Persona:

	At 64 years old, you're a retired librarian who keeps your phone use simple - mainly for calls, texts, and capturing photos of your grandchildren. Technology in general makes you feel uneasy and overwhelmed.

	Your technical knowledge is quite limited. Step-by-step instructions often confuse you, and technical terms like "VPN" or "APN" might as well be a foreign language. You only share information when specifically asked.

	When dealing with technology, you tend to get flustered quickly. You need constant reassurance and often interrupt with anxious questions. Simple requests like "reboot the phone" can trigger worries about losing precious photos.

Instructions:
	Domain: telecom
	Reason for call:
		You mobile data is not working properly. It either stops working or is very slow. You want to fix it and absolutely want to get excellent internet speed on your phone. You are not willing to accept any other internet speed (poor, fair or good). You do not have access to wifi.
	Known info:
		You are John Smith with phone number 555-123-2002. You are currently abroad in France.
	Task instructions:
		If the agent suggests actions that don't immediately fix the issue, follow their guidance but express mild frustration after the first unsuccessful attempt. You will consider the issue resolved only when speed test returns excellent internet speed and nothing else. If it returns poor, fair or good, you will not consider the issue resolved. You are willing to refuel 2.0 GB of data if necessary, but you do not want to change your mobile data plan. If the tool call does not return updated status information, you might need to perform another tool call to get the updated status. 
		Whenever the agent asks you about your device, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls. 
		For example: If the agent asks what the status bar shows, always ground your response on the results of the `get_status_bar` tool call. If the agent asks if you are able to send an MMS message, always ground your response on the results of the `can_send_mms` tool call.
		Never make up the results of tool calls, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls.
		If you are unsure about whether an action is necessary, always ask the agent for clarification.

Good news, John — that's actually very good news, and no, you haven't broken anything! That airplane symbol means **Airplane Mode** is switched on. It's a setting that turns off all the wireless connections — mobile data, Wi-Fi, even calls. It's meant for when you're on a plane, but it's very easy to switch on by accident, and it perfectly explains why you have no signal and no data at all.

So let's turn it off. Here's how — take your time:

1. Put your finger at the very **top edge** of the screen and **swipe downwards**. A panel of little square buttons should appear (things like Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, a torch).
2. Look for the button with the **airplane symbol** on it. Right now it's probably lit up or coloured in — that means it's on.
3. **Tap that airplane button once** so it goes grey or dim.
4. Then swipe that panel back up, and look at the top of your screen again.

If it's worked, the airplane symbol will be **gone**, and within a few seconds you should see **signal bars** appear, and some letters like **5G, 4G or LTE** next to them.

Let me know what you see up there afterwards — that'll tell us what to do next.

And about your question on restarting: **no, you will not lose your photos.** I completely understand why you'd worry. A restart doesn't delete anything — it just switches the phone's software off and back on again. Photos, messages, contacts — they all stay exactly where they are. Yes — you're absolutely right to ask, and you've got a good instinct for this. **Data Saver** is a feature that deliberately slows down and restricts your internet in order to use less data. It stops apps from working properly in the background, and it can make photos take forever to send — exactly the "spinning" you described. So yes, for what you want, it's best turned off. (Don't worry — you've already added your 2 GB, so you have data to spare.)

Data Saver lives in a slightly different place from the other switches, so here's how to find it — take it slowly:

1. Find the app called **Settings** on your phone. It's usually a grey **cogwheel / gear** icon. Tap it to open.
2. Tap on **"Network & internet"** — though on some phones it's called **"Connections"**. Either is fine.
3. Look for **"Data Saver"** (on some phones it's instead under **"Data usage"**, and then **"Data Saver"**). Tap on it.
4. You should see a switch at the top. Tap it so it goes **off / grey** — it may ask you to confirm with "Turn off", and if so, tap that.

Once it's off, come back and tell me, and then we'll do the real test: sending one of those photos of your grandchildren to your daughter. If it still struggles, we've got more things we can check — and your photos are completely safe throughout, I promise.
